Resolves #20421

🌿 A nested effect can no longer end the pause it runs inside.

`EffectManager`'s tracking pause was a boolean. `Effect.run()` brackets its own `isRunning` bookkeeping with the same `pauseTracking()`/`resumeTracking()` pair, so the first effect that ran inside an untracked region ended it, and the outer effect subscribed to everything it read afterwards. The pause is now a counter that belongs to the active effect: `push()` starts a pushed effect at 0, so it still tracks its own reads, and `pop()` restores the outer effect's pause. `isTrackingPaused` is a getter over the counter.

Evidence: L2 (Node unit arms, red on `dev`, green here) → L2 required (every AC is unit-observable). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 — untracked read after a nested run creates no dependency | CI-covered: `core/Effect.spec.mjs` › "A nested Effect run keeps an outer pauseTracking() region untracked"; red on `dev` (2 runs, expected 1) |
| AC-2 — tracked reads still subscribe | CI-covered: the same arm (`tracked.set(2)` re-runs), plus the existing Effect and EffectBatching specs |
| AC-3 — an Effect created inside a pause tracks its own reads | CI-covered: `core/Effect.spec.mjs` › "An Effect that runs inside a pauseTracking() region still tracks its own reads"; `functional/UseMemo.spec.mjs:154` |
| AC-4 — a bound write that runs an Effect leaves the formatter independent | CI-covered: `state/Provider.spec.mjs` › "A bound write whose afterSet runs an Effect leaves the formatter independent of its later reads"; red on `dev` (formatter ran 4 times, expected 3) |
| AC-5 — an unmatched resume cannot go below 0 | CI-covered: `core/Effect.spec.mjs` › "An unmatched resumeTracking() leaves the next pause intact" |
| AC-6 — `isTrackingPaused` reads; full unit suite green | CI-covered: the unit job; local full suite in Test Evidence |

## Deltas from ticket

- The pause is scoped to the effect stack frame (`push()`/`pop()`). The ticket body is amended with why: a global counter alone reddened `UseMemo.spec.mjs:154`.
- The Provider arm lives in `state/Provider.spec.mjs`, beside the binding behaviour it covers.

## Test Evidence

- Both new behaviour arms are red on `dev` `f82061f2c9` and green on this head.
- The global-counter variant (no `push()`/`pop()` scope) reddened `UseMemo.spec.mjs:154`: the memoized child showed `one` instead of `two`. This head is green there.
- Local full unit suite at this head: **6,110 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed** in 3.9 min (`--workers=1`, `NEO_MCP_REMOTE_TOKEN` unset).
- The downstream whitebox e2e from the ticket's Context no longer hangs on this head. The store call settles at 8 rows, and every cell assertion of its pivot step passes. Its next step fails on a separate store defect, now with that store's owner.
- `agent-preflight`: not hosted here; the baseline jobs run in CI.
